bull_bear.body: Debt repayment of INR 195cr completed from IPO proceeds; Focus on organic greenfield growth (60 centers); Merger with subsidiary (AEHL) expected completion by Q3 FY27 (5-6 months post-July EGM).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk in doubling North/West expansion; Regulatory delays in clinical licenses impacting real estate acquisition; Integration risks in pending merger; High paramedical attrition (25%); Concentration risk in South region (61% revenue).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasized 'disciplined expansion' and 'operating leverage'; Transparent on new center losses (INR 30cr) as strategic investment; Bullish on premiumization sustainability.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: In-house 'Neo' AI-ready HMS platform managing 20k patients/day built to scale to 5k branches; Own optometry schools mitigate industry-wide talent shortage; Clinical Board ensures standardization across 269 facilities despite rapid geographic dispersion; Femto cataract growth (87%) outpacing overall cataract volume (14%) indicates rapid technology adoption curve.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Consolidated balance sheet is presented as net cash: Gross Debt Rs 152 Cr (LT 120, ST 33) against cash and equivalents of Rs 214 Cr, giving Net Debt/(Cash) of Rs (62) Cr in the latest column - though the same table carries two contradictory sets of period headers (see notes).
- Listed subsidiary Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital Ltd (AEHL) is also net cash, with Net Debt/(Cash) of Rs (12) Cr as on Q1'FY27 versus Rs (14) Cr as on Q4'FY26; AEHL's other investments are stated to follow "receipt of funds from the preferential allotment".
- Return metrics disclosed for FY25 and FY26: Return on Capital Employed 16.0% and 16.6%; Return on Equity 6.8% and 8.2%; CFO/EBITDA 71.7% and 84.5%; Net Debt/EBITDA 1.4x and 1.5x.
- Shareholding as on Jun 30, 2026: Promoters 32.3%, TPG 23.1% (via Hyperion Investments Pte. Ltd), Temasek 20.1% (via Claymore Investments (Mauritius) Pte. Ltd. and Arvon Investments Pte. Ltd.), FIIs 14.8%, DIIs 7.7%, Non-Institutions 2.0%; largest other institutional holder GIC at 6.4%.
- No dividend policy, buyback, capex budget or funding plan is disclosed anywhere in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Surgical Services: 67% of revenue, 323k surgeries (+14.5% YoY), Cataract 73% mix (High-end 26.3%, Femto +87%); Refractive 5% mix (SMILE +19%); Non-Surgical (Diagnosis/Consult): 12%; Optical/Pharmacy: 21%. Region: South 61% (+22.6%), West 16% (+19%), North 9% (+20.7%).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Claims to be India's largest eye care services chain and "#1 Eye Care Services Provider in India by Revenue" per Crisil Intelligence: revenue of Rs 1,711 Cr (revenue as on March 31, 2025) against Peer #1 at Rs 1,113 Cr and Peer #2 at Rs 573 Cr.
- Largest eye care network by surgical facilities per Crisil: 199 surgical facilities versus Peer #1 at 168 and Peer #2 at 83 (for Peer #2 the count excludes 200 vision centres under a PPP model).
- Five stated "Key Pillars": largest geographically diversified chain; attractive financial performance and improving operating profitability (over FY22-FY26); scalable asset-light hub-and-spoke model; qualified medical team; proven organic growth plus integration of acquisitions; doctor-promoters with experienced management and board; proven clinical excellence.
- Entry barriers cited for the sector: ~1.5 ophthalmologists per 100k people in India against a requirement of c.8.7 eye care professionals per 100k (as of FY25), brand equity, SOP/operational expertise, and technology upgrade needs that may lead to higher capex.
- Deck says the company has the "Highest Number of NABH Accredited Facilities Amongst Eye Care Players in India" at 60, including eight NABH facilities under renewal.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group structure] Dr. Agarwal's Health Care Ltd holds 72.7% of listed Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital Ltd (27.3% public), 100% of Orbit Healthcare Services (Mauritius) Ltd which runs the Africa business and has 9 step-down subsidiaries, 100% of Aditya Jyot Eye Hospital Private Limited (balance 12.25% stake acquired in October 2025), 93.2% of Elisar Life Sciences Private Limited and 51.0% of Dr Thind Eye Care Private Limited (as on Mar 31, 2026, updated for the preferential allotment).
- [Closures] Two primary facilities were closed in Q1'FY27 - Janipur (Jammu) and Zirakpur (Punjab); in FY26, five primary facilities were closed.
- [Industry] Crisil-sourced market framing: India healthcare delivery market c. Rs 7.7 Lakh Cr growing 10-12% FY26-FY30P; India single specialty healthcare c. Rs 2.7-3.5 Lakh Cr; India eye care services market c. Rs 48,500 Cr growing 12-14% FY26E-FY30P, with eye care the fastest-growing single specialty (14% FY20-FY25 versus 6-8% to 10-12% for dental, mother-and-child, oncology and orthopaedic).
- [Payor mix] Q1'FY27 payor mix was Cash 63.6%, Insurance/TPA 27.7% and Government 8.7% (versus 61.7% / 29.1% / 9.2% in Q1'FY26); payor-mix revenue excludes subsidiary Elisar Life Sciences.
- [Elisar] Multiple disclosures (vintage performance, mature/emerging split, payor mix, regional mix) explicitly exclude revenues of subsidiary Elisar Life Sciences Private Limited, which is engaged in developing, designing, manufacturing, importing and exporting ophthalmic diagnostic devices such as auto perimeters, optical biometers and ophthalmoscopes - so those cuts do not reconcile to consolidated revenue.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin 30.2% (Q4) despite INR 30cr loss from FY26 vintage centers; Doctor/Employee costs stable at 33% of revenue; Paramedical attrition 21-25% with 9.5-10% wage inflation; New center burn expected to persist at INR 30-40cr level in FY27 due to higher surgical mix additions.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Sustained ~20-22% pace; Margin: Stable EBITDA margins despite expansion; Order Inflow: 10k daily walk-ins (+25% YoY); Capex: INR 380-400cr for 60 new facilities (40 surgical, 20 clinics) in FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Pipeline of 30 signed letters of intent for properties; Targeting 7-8 additional Delhi-NCR centers in next 12-18 months.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: North region doubling facility additions in FY27; Delhi-NCR cluster scaling from 1 to ~8 centers; Mumbai region aggressive push planned; 30% of facilities in Tier-1 vs 63% in other markets offers deep Tier-2/3 penetration runway.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Dr. Agarwal's crossed INR 2,000cr revenue with 21.6% growth driven by disciplined greenfield additions (19 in Q4) and 14% same-store growth, while margin expansion to 28.9% EBITDA proves operating leverage despite INR 30cr drag from new centers. The impending merger with the listed subsidiary and aggressive FY27 capex (60 new centers) position the company to double down on North/West expansion while sustaining premiumization trends in high-end cataract and refractive procedures.
